name: Stockholm Monsters
label: Factory Records
lede: Peter Hook produced nearly everything they made, the Burnage teenagers who'd turn into Oasis grew up watching them, and Stockholm Monsters were gone two years before Madchester arrived.

eras.title: Burnage kids, Bowie's title, Hook's ear
eras.text: Stockholm Monsters were still teenagers with no permanent guitarist when they joined the Manchester Musicians Collective. One support slot at Rafters brought Rob Gretton and Peter Hook to see them, and Hook stayed.

yt: A Room in a Tower, 1980 demo
years.h: Tony France takes a Bowie title and a capital city
years.p: [[Tony France|9656b566-51c2-47ee-8f6f-78a0f7e2bdd7]], bassist Jed Duffy and drummer [[Shan Hira|af05ba2e-72c5-4e36-8cec-203e77e7e850]] started the band in south Manchester. France built the name from Scary Monsters and Stockholm.
years.xp: Asked later where the name came from, France told an interviewer: "We thought Stockholm was a nice country." Then: "We wanted something opposite to Stockholm so we chose Monsters."

years.cap: Poster for New Order, Section 25 and Stockholm Monsters
years.h: A Rezillos support at Rafters brings [[Peter Hook|73e7c483-9f3e-4a72-a359-582452fbaeac]] to the front
years.p: [[Rob Gretton|41b55fab-da3b-4ecf-a67d-aeeec338a9c5]] and Hook came to see them and Hook became their mentor, producing nearly all their records under the name Be Music.

years.h: Shan's sister Lita Hira joins on keyboards
years.p: The band supported [[New Order|f1106b17-dcbb-45f6-b938-199ccfab50cc]] on dates across northern England.

eras.title: Hannett's single, New Order's tour bus
eras.text: The debut single sat for a year before Factory released it, then the band went to Europe with New Order and picked up a trumpet player along the way.

years.src: LTM: Stockholm Monsters · Wikipedia: Stockholm Monsters
years.h: [[Martin Hannett|ffbfce58-5185-4bcc-8c45-a7cd5d1a3783]] produces Fairy Tales, FAC 41
years.p: Delayed a year, it reached No. 43 on the indie chart. Mark Farrow's sleeve came in green or purple.
years.xp: NME's Paul Morley liked it, and ZigZag's Mick Mercer compared France's voice to Peter Gabriel's.

years.h: Lindsay Anderson brings a trumpet on New Order's European tour
years.p: She joined for New Order's April dates in France, Belgium and Holland. A 1983 interview put her age at 17.

years.h: The B-side, Soft Babies, is the one that gets a video
years.p: Happy Ever After (FAC 58) carried Soft Babies on the flip, and its clip went onto A Factory Video.

years.cap: Hacienda gig list with the Durutti Column and Stockholm Monsters, 1982
yt: Live at the Blue Note, Derby, 1982
years.h: Duffy leaves for Lavolta Lakota; Karl France takes the bass
years.p: Tony's brother [[Karl France|0ff2337d-25e0-49c1-8a52-ee2e588aba7d]] stepped in.

years.src: LTM: Stockholm Monsters · Wikipedia: Stockholm Monsters
years.h: Miss Moonlight EP on Factory Benelux
years.p: FBN 19. Another song, The Longing, went onto Factory's Shorts video collection.

years.h: A Bournemouth reviewer says they look more like roadies
years.p: The Coaster found them scruffy and stand-offish backstage. A Masterbag interviewer noticed Anderson reading a Bowie biography through the whole thing.

years.h: Lita Hira leaves; guitarist John Rhodes joins
years.p: Karl France moved to bass full time and Tony France took up guitar alongside Rhodes.

eras.title: One album, made slowly on purpose
eras.text: Alma Mater was the band's only album. Reviews ran from 'an important cog in the Factory machinery' to one of the worst things an NME writer had heard.

years.h: NME warms to All at Once
years.p: FAC 107, backed with National Pastime.

years.src: LTM: Stockholm Monsters · Wikipedia: Alma Mater
years.h: Alma Mater, Fact 80, recorded at Strawberry with Hook
years.p: Cut in January 1984 and mixed at Revolution in March. LTM puts sales at about 4,000.
years.xp:
Sounds' Dave Roberts wrote that the band was "fast becoming a very important cog in the Factory machinery." One NME reviewer called it "close to the worst thing I've ever heard."

Years later AllMusic's Stewart Mason called it a record "all but ignored at the time" that sounds prescient in hindsight. Trevor Johnson designed the sleeve.

q: We want to do it on the merit of the music, without doing interviews.
years.h: Hira and France explain why they fit Factory
years.p: Tony France, to interviewer Robert Graham: Factory suited a band that took its time. Manager Andy Fisher was less happy that the album hadn't opened more doors.

eras.title: Stolen gear and a swing at Tony Wilson
eras.text: The Monsters kept working with borrowed equipment as Happy Mondays took over Factory's attention. A punch at the Haçienda didn't help, and by 1987 the band was done.

years.src: LTM: Stockholm Monsters · Wikipedia: Stockholm Monsters
years.h: How Corrupt Is Rough Trade? names a distributor
years.p: FBN 46, with Kan Kill!, reached No. 47 on the indie chart.
years.xp: Manager Andy Fisher explained the title in 1986: Rough Trade Distribution's stock listing showed "none" of their records for months, while the band believed they could have kept selling.

years.h: Thieves clear out the rehearsal room
years.p: Nearly all the band's equipment was stolen in Manchester, and the insurance claim was disputed. They carried on with borrowed gear.

years.cap: Poster for Stockholm Monsters at the Richmond, Brighton, February 1985
years.h: NME calls them "a riot and a half" at Hammersmith's Clarendon
years.p: A Factory showcase with [[Section 25|82e26f64-813d-4b22-a442-44d182f7f9eb]], after October dates in Italy with [[The Durutti Column|aaddb5e3-f8a5-4a9d-8674-f885112ecf0e]]. [[Happy Mondays|01f4fb92-6bf0-4de5-83dc-3fe194e763bf]] were on the bill but didn't play.

years.cap: NME live review of New Order and Stockholm Monsters, January 1986
years.h: Supporting [[The Smiths|40f5d9e4-2de7-4f2d-ad41-e31a9a9fea27]] in Newcastle and Glasgow
years.p: The Monsters opened Smiths dates on the The Queen Is Dead tour.

years.h: Guitarist John Rhodes hits [[Tony Wilson|124a6f5d-b2e0-4a75-95ad-db4c38063e02]] at the Haçienda
years.p: LTM says the incident did further damage to the band's standing at Factory.

years.src: LTM: Stockholm Monsters · Wikipedia: Stockholm Monsters
years.h: Hook reworks Partyline until it changes shape
years.p: FAC 146 was produced at Cargo, by then Suite 16, where Shan Hira had become Hook's business partner. It was the band's last single.
years.xp:
LTM's James Nice says the endless reworking turned a powerful Monsters song into "a somewhat cluttered electronic concoction."

A final studio demo included Stupid and House Is Not a Home. The band split within months, two years before Madchester. Hira stayed in the studio trade, running Suite 16 in Rochdale.

eras.title: The first band from Burnage
eras.text: LTM gathered the records on CD, Noel Gallagher named them as the band that got him into music, and a Brooklyn label put them back on vinyl.

years.big: "The first band ever to come from Burnage"
years.src: LTM: Stockholm Monsters · Wikipedia: Stockholm Monsters
years.h: Noel Gallagher traces Oasis back to Burnage's first band
years.p: [[Noel Gallagher|6493ed80-8b44-49fa-91de-e7b0a0b57d6d]] said the older guys round his way were in Stockholm Monsters. From there, he said, it was [[Joy Division|9a58fda3-f4ed-4080-a3a5-f457aac9fcdd]], New Order, the Smiths, the Roses, the Mondays, then his own band.

years.src: Captured Tracks: All At Once · Wikipedia: Stockholm Monsters
years.h: Captured Tracks reissues All at Once on double vinyl
years.p: LTM had gathered the singles and archive recordings on CD in 2001; the Brooklyn label's edition put them back on vinyl.
